name: Flooring Protocol
rootCause: Flooring Protocol's NFT liquidity platform used a BT404-style hybrid token standard that blends fungible and non-fungible mechanics in a single contract. An integer overflow in the platform's token balance accounting logic enabled a "ghost ownership" attack: a malicious token ID could be used to satisfy one ownership check while simultaneously producing a different result in a second accounting path within the same transaction, allowing the attacker to artificially inflate their fpToken (the fungible claim token) balance to near-infinite levels. The attacker redeemed these inflated fpTokens against Flooring's NFT pools to claim underlying assets. Yuga Labs executed a white-hat intervention, pulling 68 NFTs (29 BAYC, 4 MAYC, 2 CryptoPunks, and others) worth ~$500K out of harm's way before the attacker could reach them; net losses were approximately $900K. The same vulnerable BT404/DN404 codebase was replicated in the Asterix fork, which was subsequently exploited for an additional ~$40K shortly afterward. Attack Tx: 0x5abc52a438734151ebd2cc122f7ae86ed04a390a6dc884f04abd679ed380aaad Analysis: 0xQuit on X

Flooring Protocol V2 and BitmapPunks (BT404 / $BMP) were exploited due to a BT404-style packed ownership logic vulnerability (malicious high-bit token ID alias + unchecked integer underflow). The attacker minted near-infinite fpTokens/$BMP with a dust amount of WETH, drained liquidity pools, and extracted high-value NFTs (e.g., BAYC, CryptoPunks) at low cost. Yuga Labs quickly intervened with a white-hat operation via GrailsOTC, rescuing 68 NFTs worth over $500,000, now held safely for return after fixes.

Flooring Protocol on Ethereum Mainnet suffered a critical accounting flaw on 8 June 2026, exposing over $500,000 in pooled NFTs to potential loss. A bug enabled unlimited minting of fpToken shares, creating a risk of draining pool assets. Yuga Labs led a documented white-hat rescue, securing 68 high-value NFTs, now in custody pending contract repair. All incident specifics are derived from technical press coverage and project participant statements; no chain forensics or official postmortem is available.
